To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

i) the genetic variability of bilberries in the investigated area was very high and the genetic structure of the populations was clonal; ii) the genetic structure was not related to the geographical location; iii) the biochemical variability of bilberries was very high and was not related to their genetic structure; iv) the biochemical variability was not related to geographical location and to genetic structure; and v) the biochemical variability in two successive harvesting periods was high and related to climate.

bilberry populations from the southernmost growing area, as well as those from Central and Northern Europe (see also the other paper of the same issue), are characterized by a gamic genetic propagation, and that, although the biochemical variability is quite high, it does not seem to be correlated with the genetic structure of populations.

the RAPD analysis of bilberries collected from the southernmost growing areas of this plant, indicated a high prevalence of gamic propagation, and suggested a clonal-to gamic genetic gradient of this propagation strategy, from North-to South Europe.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the genetic characterization of a southern population of bilberry, and with the evaluation of the biochemical diversity in the same population, in order to assess the possible relationships between genetics and phenotypic diversity.
the genetic and biochemical diversity of bilberry populations, and with their possible relationships in the southernmost area of the species distribution in Europe.
a very interesting case of bilberry populations, growing in a very southern area of its natural distribution, where the genetic variability is high and the biochemical variability is low.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genetic diversity of V. myrtillus populations from the southernmost growing area of this species in Italy is not reflected by the biochemical diversity of their fruits.

the genetic variability of bilberry populations in the southernmost growing areas is mainly due to clonal propagation, while environmental conditions are the major factor influencing the variability of biochemical attributes.

, in this study, genetic variability did not play a major role in the observed variations of the biochemical traits, and that the observed variability of these traits was mainly due to environmental factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genetic diversity and biochemical variability of bilberries are mainly due to climatic conditions.
the RAPD analysis of V. myrtillus L., in spite of its high level of polymorphism, does not provide information about the biochemical diversity of this plant.
the southernmost growing area of bilberry in Italy is characterized by a very homogeneous genetic structure, but also by a remarkable variability of biochemical attributes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the southernmost part of the distribution range of bilberry, this species shows a very high genetic variability, which may be related to its ability to colonize a very heterogeneous environment.
the southernmost populations of bilberries are genetically highly homogeneous, and that the biochemical variability of the berries is not related to genetic diversity.

bilberries growing at the southernmost limit of the species distribution in Europe exhibit a high genetic diversity, which may be exploited for the selection of genotypes with high content of bioactive molecules.
